# Major ICT-related incident classification

<!-- Generated by `python -m dora_roi.docs`; do not edit by hand. -->

Criteria of DORA Art. 18 as specified by the RTS on classification (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772) and reporting time limits (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301), as implemented by `roi incidents` and the *Incidents* screen of the workbench. Thresholds and article numbers are open assumptions (A-INC-* in [ASSUMPTIONS.md](ASSUMPTIONS.md)); every value is a field of `dora_roi.incidents.criteria.Thresholds`.

**Major incident** = *critical services affected* **and** either a successful, malicious, unauthorised access to network and information systems that may result in data losses, **or** the thresholds of **two or more** of the six other criteria met.

| Criterion | DORA | RTS | Materiality threshold |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical services affected | DORA Art. 18(1)(e) | RTS Art. 6 | Gate: required for a major incident. |
| Clients, financial counterparts and transactions | DORA Art. 18(1)(a) | RTS Art. 1, Art. 9(1) | > 10 % of clients of the service, or > 100,000 clients, or > 30 % of financial counterparts, or > 10 % of the daily number or > 10 % of the daily value of transactions, or relevant clients/counterparts affected. |
| Reputational impact | DORA Art. 18(1)(a) | RTS Art. 2, Art. 9(2) | Any of: media coverage, repeated complaints, regulatory requirements not met, likely loss of clients or counterparts. |
| Duration and service downtime | DORA Art. 18(1)(b) | RTS Art. 3, Art. 9(3) | Duration > 24 h, or downtime of services supporting critical functions > 2 h. |
| Geographical spread | DORA Art. 18(1)(c) | RTS Art. 4, Art. 9(4) | Impact in 2 or more Member States. |
| Data losses | DORA Art. 18(1)(d) | RTS Art. 5, Art. 9(5) | Any such impact on data. |
| Economic impact | DORA Art. 18(1)(f) | RTS Art. 7, Art. 9(6) | Costs and losses > EUR 100,000. |

## Unknown answers

Every answer may be *unknown*. The outcome is computed with all unknowns as "not met" and as "met"; it is **major** or **not major** only when both agree, otherwise **undetermined** with the list of open questions that could change it. An ongoing incident's duration counts from occurrence (or awareness) to now and is not final.

## Recurring incidents

Individually non-major incidents with the same apparent root cause (same recurrence key) that occurred at least twice within 6 months are combined: counts, durations, downtime and costs are added, totals use the largest denominator, yes/no answers are true if any is true, Member States are united. If the combination is major, the series is flagged for reporting as one major incident.

## Reporting time limits

| Report | Due |
|---|---|
| Initial notification | 4 h after classification as major, at the latest 24 h after becoming aware |
| Intermediate report | 72 h after the initial notification (projected from its deadline until it is submitted) |
| Final report | 1 month after the intermediate report (projected likewise) |

Weekend and bank-holiday relief is not applied (conservative).
